prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create a polished landscape Chinese engineering progress infographic for a Python-to-Go migration iteration. Clear large Chinese typography, restrained editorial layout, pale neutral background, dark readable text, blue for completed requests, amber for observed differences, subtle dividers. No brand logos, no decorative characters. All quantitative lengths must faithfully encode the supplied counts. Render Chinese labels verbatim and sharply.

Title: "Go 迁移｜Provider URL 范围核对"
Subtitle: "34 种 URL · 68 个 direct / SSE 观察"
Top workflow with four stages: "实际 Python provider + SDK" → "冻结 Source 契约" → "Go 诊断观察" → "差异分类"

Central comparison: two horizontal bars, each totals 68.
Source: "52 完成" + "10 请求期失败" + "6 构造拒绝".
Go: "36 完成" + "32 构造拒绝".
Label these as request-construction observations through injected HTTP boundaries, not real-network success.

Lower left panel title: "双方完成的 36 个观察"
Show "22 一致" and "14 差异".
Below: "主机 / 端口 / IDNA：12"
Below: "空 fragment 表示：2".

Lower right panel title: "Go 构造拒绝的 32 个观察"
Show "双方构造拒绝：6"
Show "Source 可构造、Go 拒绝：26".
Mention "query / userinfo / 相对路径等既有边界".

Footer delivery strip:
"新增：68 个冻结观察 · Source 契约测试 · Go 诊断工具 · 差异清单"
"验证：provider race、vet、19 项扫描守卫通过"
"全量 Go：background 结果差异、reload 超时仍开放"
Final important scope label: "本轮未修改运行时 URL 规则；完整迁移尚未完成"
Tiny date label: "2026-10-11".

Constraints: Do not claim all tests passed, URL parity achieved, real network acceptance, or migration complete. Do not show an overall completion percentage. No extra invented numbers. Keep text concise; use ample whitespace. This is a change-summary infographic, not a dashboard screenshot.
edit: Edit this infographic. Preserve every Chinese and English text label, count, title, subtitle, date, footer, overall layout, colors and typography exactly. Correct a quantitative-design issue: the stacked bar lengths currently do not faithfully represent the counts. Replace ONLY the four stacked bars (Source 52/10/6, Go 36/32, both-completed 22/14, Go-constructor-refused 6/26) with sets of equal-width separate rectangular number cards. These cards are category labels, NOT measured bars: use equal widths within each set, with small whitespace gaps. Keep each existing count and its label centered in its own card. Preserve the surrounding panels and headings. No progress bars, no stacked bar segments, no quantitative area encoding, no extra numbers or percentage labels. Keep everything else unchanged and maintain the same landscape dimensions.
